storyboard.claim: The inventor generates many ideas and discards the bad ones instantly, without testing them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor speaking in his workshop; the callout names the act of throwing out the junk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Rabino example: his expertise lets him filter as he goes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows filtering happens in the head, not on paper.

storyboard.claim: His mind is saturated with the rules of his domain, so he knows which ideas break physics or cannot be machined.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor thinking with a book in hand: the domain's rulebook he has absorbed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the filtering in beat 40 works.
storyboard.addedInformation: The book is the domain's knowledge, not a literal reading of thermodynamics.

storyboard.claim: If creativity needs surplus attention, is it elitist?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host posing the question; no icon, because any icon would answer it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts open the objection raised by the previous claim.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the question on screen so the viewer knows the argument is being tested.

storyboard.claim: Only the wealthy or privileged have the free time to become innovators.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door icon: the way into innovation, shut to people without free time.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The elitism question from beat 42, stated as a concrete exclusion.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door reads as exclusion; the callout names who is excluded.

callout.text: Three jobs just to pay rent

storyboard.claim: A person working three jobs to pay rent has no surplus attention.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worn-out worker slumped with a wallet: money squeezing time and energy.
storyboard.onScreenText: Three jobs just to pay rent
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The critique from beat 43, turned into a person.
storyboard.addedInformation: Worried plus slump reads as exhaustion, not alarm.

storyboard.claim: The system favors people who have access, and rent takes the attention of those who do not.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host agreeing; no icon, the callout carries the claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Confirms the critique from beat 44 and sets up the reply.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: the narrator is the only figure on screen, so the point rests on the callout.

storyboard.claim: Exhaustion from survival drains the surplus attention creativity needs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tired worker slumped in sadness, the body showing depletion.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the rent point as a cost to attention.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sad plus slump shows depletion; the callout names the cause.

storyboard.claim: Financial wealth and specialized attention are different things.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-bucket sorter: financial wealth on one side, specialized attention on the other.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The distinction the hosts promise after the rent objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the split between money and attention visible as two separate buckets.

storyboard.claim: A penniless teenage refugee crossing a war-torn continent had no financial privilege.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A young man walking with a war icon behind him: the refugee's journey through war.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the case that answers the wealth question from beat 47.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon reads literally as war; the callout gives the status.

storyboard.claim: What he had was obsessive specialization of whatever attention he possessed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A focused young man thinking, with a target icon: attention aimed at one point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the refugee example from beat 48.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target reads as aim and focus, which is the claim.

storyboard.claim: In a complex world, specialized knowledge is favored over general knowledge, and wealth is not the point.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host explaining; no icon, since a money icon would contradict the negated wealth claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises the refugee example into a rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: the rejected wealth idea is only in the spoken line, not staged.

storyboard.claim: In the system metaphor, the person is the spark.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lightbulb icon for the spark of a new idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the spark and kindling metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lightbulb reads as an idea; the callout names the person as the spark.

storyboard.claim: The domain (kindling) must be mastered: its rules, history and math, before the spark can catch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A book icon for the rules, history and math of the domain.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the metaphor from the spark to the kindling.
storyboard.addedInformation: The book reads as study and knowledge, which matches the claim.

storyboard.claim: Having a spark and kindling is not enough; this is the first gear's limit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking; no icon, the callout carries the limit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the first gear and sets up the second, the field.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: nothing is staged to show what the second gear is yet.

storyboard.claim: The gatekeepers, the field of experts, decide who gets in.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gatekeeper pointing angrily at a door: the field as the one who blocks entry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the second gear, the field.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry plus point shows a threat of rejection, the dreaded part the narrator names.

storyboard.claim: An editor at a late-night desk is overwhelmed by manuscripts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An exhausted editor slumped at an office desk piled high.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the editor the hosts describe.
storyboard.addedInformation: Worried plus slump reads as overwhelmed, not shocked.

storyboard.claim: The editor stares at an 800-page manuscript from an unknown author.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A book icon for the manuscript, with the editor thinking over it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the editor scene from beat 55.
storyboard.addedInformation: The book reads as the manuscript being judged.

storyboard.claim: The author spent years mapping stars, weather and sailing distances from the Odyssey.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A compass icon for navigation and sailing research.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the author's manuscript from beat 56.
storyboard.addedInformation: The compass reads as navigation, the sailing research in the book.

storyboard.claim: The author's manuscript tries to prove that Ulysses sailed around Florida.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking; no icon, the callout states the absurd claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals what the research was trying to prove.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout carries the absurdity; no icon is needed.

storyboard.claim: The editor drops the manuscript straight into the recycling bin.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The editor holding a book, indifferent, the manuscript about to be thrown away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The outcome of beats 55 to 58.
storyboard.addedInformation: Blank face reads as indifference, the dismissal the narrator describes.

storyboard.claim: Meanwhile the author sits at home, convinced of a world-changing genius.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A home icon with a sad, seated artist in a living room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the editor's rejection with the author at home.
storyboard.addedInformation: The home icon reads literally as a house; sad face shows the heartbreak.

storyboard.claim: The author is sure they are a misunderstood genius.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A painter celebrating with confidence, the self-belief the narrator describes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the author's situation from beat 60.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: the self-belief is shown by pose, not by a symbol.

storyboard.claim: Personal brilliance or certainty is not enough to change culture.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking; the callout carries the rule.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Draws the lesson from the author's certainty in beat 61.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the rule that the field decides, not the person.

storyboard.claim: An idea is not creative in the historical sense until the field of experts accepts it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gatekeeper holding a key: the field decides who is let in.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the condition to the lesson from beat 62.
storyboard.addedInformation: The key reads as access granted by the field.

storyboard.claim: An idea the gatekeepers do not validate vanishes, and history treats it as a delusion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host with a fearful face; no icon, since a literal void or grave would mislead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The consequence of beat 63.
storyboard.addedInformation: Afraid face shows the stakes the narrator calls terrifying.

storyboard.claim: The Nobel economist George Stigler explains the brutal numbers of the field.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An expert-panel figure talking, standing in for the expert who sets the numbers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the numbers that follow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: the named person is not in the story bible, so a gatekeeper stands in for the expert.

storyboard.claim: A journal with 7,000 subscribers: just 15 peers reading a paper carefully is a success.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The expert figure beside the numbers, with no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the numbers Stigler mentions.
storyboard.addedInformation: The numbers are carried by the callout, not a picture.

storyboard.claim: Fifteen readers out of 7,000 is called a massive runaway success.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy icon for the prize of being called a success.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates beat 66 as a success.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trophy reads as a prize, which is the success the narrator names.

storyboard.claim: You are not entitled to a warm reception; you must earn it, and the field filters.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cold, unmoved gatekeeper: no welcome.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The field as a filter, from beat 67.
storyboard.addedInformation: Blank face shows the absence of a warm reception, not warmth.

storyboard.claim: The field acts like a bouncer, deciding who gets in.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gatekeeper pointing, like a bouncer choosing who enters.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the filter from beat 68 a concrete image.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: a bouncer is only read from the callout, not the staging.

callout.text: Their job is to be skeptical

storyboard.claim: The gatekeepers' evolutionary function is to be deeply skeptical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gatekeeper thinking, skeptical in posture.
storyboard.onScreenText: Their job is to be skeptical
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the bouncer in beat 69.
storyboard.addedInformation: Skepticism is named in the callout; the face stays neutral.

storyboard.claim: The field is a spam filter for human culture.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A phone icon for the inbox the host filters every day.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the field a modern comparison.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone reads as a modern inbox, which fits the analogy.

storyboard.claim: Most emails are promotions or garbage; occasionally one is important.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking about the inbox; no icon, the callout carries it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the spam filter analogy from beat 71.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: the inbox is only described, not shown.

storyboard.claim: The gatekeepers are culture's spam filter, protecting it from junk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon for the field protecting culture's rules.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects the spam filter analogy to the gatekeepers.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield reads as protection, the field's role.

callout.text: Boss's email into the junk folder

storyboard.claim: The spam filter can wrongly throw a boss's email into the junk folder, like gatekeepers defending the status quo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking; no icon, the callout names the mistake.
storyboard.onScreenText: Boss's email into the junk folder
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection that gatekeepers defend the status quo.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the error; the speaker does not endorse it.

storyboard.claim: Critics famously ignored Van Gogh while he was alive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A painter alone at an easel, sad, unrecognised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives a historical case for the objection in beat 74.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sad painter at an easel shows the neglect the callout names.

storyboard.claim: Without the spam filter, culture would dissolve into chaos.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking; no icon, to avoid a literal storm or weather reading.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The macro-level reply to the objection in beat 74.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: the chaos is only stated, not shown.

storyboard.claim: Consider the arithmetic of human production.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host thinking about the numbers, with no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the numbers in beat 78.
storyboard.addedInformation: Invites the viewer to think about the scale.

storyboard.claim: Hundreds of thousands of people in the US consider themselves artists.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A single painter standing for the many artists, no crowd repeat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The scale from beat 77.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: one figure stands for many; the number is carried by the callout.

storyboard.claim: If each painted one picture a year, that would be millions of new paintings every year, more than museums can process.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worried painter thinking, with the stacked callout showing the pile of paintings.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The consequence of the math in beats 77 and 78.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stack style shows accumulation; worried plus think reads as overwhelm.
